rest.catalog.answers.parseError: Any endpoint that reads a body (creating or updating a product or a category), when the body is not valid JSON. `message` carries the parser's own words and the position. Nothing was changed; correct the body before sending it again.
rest.catalog.answers.notAnObject: Any endpoint that reads a body, when the body is valid JSON but not an object: an array, a string, a number or `null`. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.answers.tooManyFields: Any endpoint, when the query string carries more than 1,000 parameters, or a URL-encoded or `multipart/form-data` body more than 1,000 fields. Nothing was read or changed; no valid catalog request comes near this.
rest.catalog.answers.filesNotAccepted: Any endpoint that reads a body (creating or updating a product or a category), when the body is `multipart/form-data` and one of its parts is a file: its `Content-Disposition` names a `filename` that is not empty. Catalog takes no files, so it stops at that part instead of reading the file; nothing was created or changed. Send the fields as JSON, and an image as an `image_url` link. The token, and for a category the `admin` role, are checked first; for a product this answer comes before identity is asked about the merchant. Parts are read in order, so text fields before the first file that break the size or count limit answer `413` `BODY_TOO_LARGE` or `400` `TOO_MANY_FIELDS` instead. A form of text fields only, or a part whose `filename` is empty, is read as text as before.
rest.catalog.answers.noToken: Any endpoint that needs a token (`GET /api/v1/products/mine` and every write), when the request has no `Authorization` header, or one that is not `Bearer` followed by a single token. Sign in and send the access token.
rest.catalog.answers.invalidToken: Any endpoint that needs a token, when the token is refused: its signature, issuer or audience is wrong, it has expired, it names no signing key or one that identity does not publish, or it is not an access token (a refresh token or a two-factor challenge token is refused here). Refresh the token pair and retry once with the new access token.
rest.catalog.answers.unknownPath: Any path under `/api/v1/products` or `/api/v1/categories` that names no endpoint, such as an `{id}` that is not all digits, or one segment too many. Every catalog endpoint answers with or without a trailing slash: `/api/v1/categories` and `/api/v1/categories/` are the same request.
rest.catalog.answers.methodNotAllowed: Any catalog path, with a method it does not take; `Allow` lists the methods it does. Products are created at `POST /api/v1/products/create`, not at `/api/v1/products`. A token that is sent is verified first (with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`, and on `/api/v1/products/mine` with any method), so an invalid one answers `401` instead.
rest.catalog.answers.notAcceptable: Any endpoint, when the `Accept` header names no type that `application/json` satisfies. Catalog answers only JSON: send `Accept: application/json`, or no `Accept` at all. A `format` query parameter chooses nothing and is ignored.
rest.catalog.answers.bodyTooLarge: Any endpoint that reads a body, when a JSON or URL-encoded body, or the text fields of a `multipart/form-data` body taken together, are larger than 2,621,440 bytes (2.5 MiB). Nothing was read or changed. No valid catalog body comes near this: an image is sent as an `image_url` link, never uploaded.
rest.catalog.answers.unsupportedMediaTyp: Any endpoint that reads a body, when a body is sent with a `Content-Type` other than `application/json`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `multipart/form-data`, or with none. Send `Content-Type: application/json`.
rest.catalog.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that catalog did not expect, such as an error the database answered with. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`, which Kong sets when the client sends none; an id longer than 128 characters, or holding anything but letters, digits and `._:#/+=-`, is not used and `traceId` reads `-`. A read can be retried; for a write, read the product or category back before retrying.
rest.catalog.answers.databaseUnavailable: Any endpoint, public reads included, when catalog cannot reach its database: the connection failed or broke, or the database is shutting down, starting up or out of connections. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds. A read is safe to retry; for a write, read the product or category back first, because a connection that broke while committing may have committed.
rest.catalog.answers.keysUnavailable: Any endpoint that needs a token, when catalog cannot fetch identity's signing keys to check it: identity did not answer, or published no usable key. The token was not judged; retry later with the same token.
rest.catalog.listProducts.summary: Lists the products on sale, newest first, one page at a time, each with its stock as warehouse reports it. Withdrawn products are left out. Products created in the same instant are ordered by `id`, highest first, so pages neither repeat nor skip a product while the catalogue does not change.
rest.catalog.listProducts.who: Anyone. The endpoint does not read the `Authorization` header, so a missing, expired or forged token changes nothing.
rest.catalog.listProducts.field.category: A category `slug`, matched exactly. Blank is ignored. No NUL character.
rest.catalog.listProducts.field.q: Matched against the title as a substring, ignoring case; not trimmed. Blank is ignored. No NUL character. Ranked search across title, category and description is `GET /api/v1/products/search`.
rest.catalog.listProducts.field.page: ASCII digits only, 1 to 10,000; default `1`. A page past the last one answers an empty `results`.
rest.catalog.listProducts.case.listed: The page. `count` is how many products match, over all pages. `category` is the category's name and `category_slug` its slug. `price` is a decimal string in rupiah with two decimals. `weight_grams` is `null` on a product created before weights were required. Stock is warehouse's: a product warehouse keeps no record for reads `0`, `false` and `out_of_stock`. A merchant that may no longer trade keeps its products listed; order's checkout refuses them.
rest.catalog.listProducts.case.stockUnkn: Warehouse did not answer for a merchant on the page, or catalog is leaving it alone for 15 seconds after three failures in a row. That merchant's products are still listed, with `available_stock` and `is_in_stock` set to `null` and `stock_status` to `unknown`, which does not mean out of stock.
rest.catalog.listProducts.case.invalid: A query parameter breaks its rule. Only the first one is reported, in the order `category`, `q`, `page`, `page_size`; `field` names it.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.summary: Lists the caller's own products, withdrawn ones included, newest first (ties by `id`, highest first), one page at a time, each in the shape a create answers. This is how a seller finds its products and their `id`s again. Stock is not included: `GET /api/v1/products/{sku}` gives it for a product on sale.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.who: A signed-in account whose token carries the `role` `seller`. It answers only the products created with that account. Identity is not asked, so a seller whose merchant awaits approval, or is suspended or closed, still sees its products.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.field.catego: A category `slug`, matched exactly. Blank is ignored. No NUL character.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.field.q: Matched against the title as a substring, ignoring case; not trimmed. Blank is ignored. No NUL character.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.field.page: ASCII digits only, 1 to 10,000; default `1`. A page past the last one answers an empty `results`.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.case.listed: The page. `count` is how many of the caller's products match, over all pages. `is_active` is `false` on a withdrawn product: it is not listed publicly or read by SKU, and `is_active` `true` on `PUT /api/v1/products/manage/{id}` puts it back on sale. `id` addresses a product in the update and withdraw endpoints. `weight_grams` is `null` on a product created before weights were required; set one with the update endpoint.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.case.invalid: A query parameter breaks its rule. Only the first one is reported, in the order `category`, `q`, `page`, `page_size`; `field` names it. The role is checked first, so this answer means the caller is a seller.
rest.catalog.listMyProducts.case.notSell: The token is valid, but its `role` is not `seller`: a buyer, courier or admin account has no products of its own.
rest.catalog.getProduct.summary: Reads one product on sale by its SKU, with its description and its stock in warehouse.
rest.catalog.getProduct.who: Anyone. The endpoint does not read the `Authorization` header.
rest.catalog.getProduct.field.sku: The SKU exactly as created; case counts. Percent-encode characters a path segment cannot carry. `create` and `mine` name other endpoints, and a SKU starting with `search` or `suggest` reaches the search service instead, which is why catalog refuses such SKUs at create.
rest.catalog.getProduct.case.found: The product. `warehouse_stock` is warehouse's record for this SKU and merchant: `available_quantity` can still be sold, `reserved_quantity` is held for orders. A product warehouse keeps no record for reads an empty `bin_location`, `0` for both quantities and `out_of_stock`.
rest.catalog.getProduct.case.stockUnknow: Warehouse did not answer, or catalog is leaving it alone for 15 seconds after three failures in a row. The product is still returned; `bin_location`, `available_quantity` and `reserved_quantity` are `null` and `stock_status` is `unknown`.
rest.catalog.getProduct.case.notFound: No product on sale has this SKU: none ever had it, or its merchant withdrew the product.
rest.catalog.createProduct.summary: Puts a new product on sale for the caller's merchant. Its SKU is permanent: it cannot be changed, and it stays taken after the product is withdrawn.
rest.catalog.createProduct.who: A signed-in account that identity knows as a merchant allowed to trade, which means an admin has approved it (`verified` or `active`). Catalog asks identity on every write; the token's `role` does not decide.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.sku: Required. Trimmed, then 1 to 64 characters with no whitespace, no `/` and no NUL character. Not `create`, `mine`, `.` or `..`, and not starting with `search` or `suggest`, because such a product page could not be reached. Unique across every merchant, withdrawn products included.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.title: Required. Text, trimmed, not blank, at most 255 characters; no NUL character.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.descrip: Optional. Text of any length, stored as sent; `null` or absent stores an empty description. No NUL character.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.price: Required. Rupiah, as a JSON number or a decimal string: more than 0, at most `9999999999.99`, with at most two decimal places. A larger value is refused however it is written, `1e30` included. Answered as a decimal string with two decimals.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.currenc: Optional. Only `IDR` is taken; `null` or absent means `IDR`.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.image_u: Optional. An `http` or `https` URL with a host, at most 200 characters, stored as given; `null`, an empty string or absent stores none. Catalog does not upload, fetch or presign images, so host the image first. A `multipart/form-data` body that carries a file is refused with `400` `FILES_NOT_ACCEPTED`.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.categor: Required. The `id` of an existing category, as a JSON integer or a string of digits.
rest.catalog.createProduct.field.weight_: Required, because shipping is priced by weight. Whole grams from 1 to 1,000,000, as a JSON integer or a string of digits.
rest.catalog.createProduct.case.created: The product is on sale. Keep `id`: it addresses the product in `/api/v1/products/manage/{id}`, and `GET /api/v1/products/mine` lists it again. Search finds the product after its next sync. Warehouse holds no stock for it until the merchant receives some.
rest.catalog.createProduct.case.invalid: A field breaks its rule. Fields are checked in the order `sku`, `title`, `description`, `price`, `currency`, `image_url`, `category_id`, `weight_grams`, and only the first broken rule is reported, in `field` and `message`. Identity has not been asked yet.
rest.catalog.createProduct.case.unknownC: `category_id` is well formed, but no category has it. `GET /api/v1/categories` lists the ones that exist.
rest.catalog.createProduct.case.notMerch: Identity knows no merchant for this account, so it cannot sell. Nothing was created.
rest.catalog.createProduct.case.mayNotSe: The account's merchant may not trade: it still awaits an admin's approval, or it is suspended or closed; `message` names its standing. Nothing was created.
rest.catalog.createProduct.case.skuTaken: Another product already has this SKU, possibly a withdrawn one, which keeps it. Choose another SKU; to sell your own withdrawn product again, find it in `GET /api/v1/products/mine` and send `is_active` `true` to its update endpoint instead.
rest.catalog.createProduct.case.identity: Catalog could not learn the merchant's standing: identity failed or did not answer within 5 seconds, or catalog is leaving it alone for 15 seconds after three failures in a row. Nothing was created; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.summary: Changes the fields sent on one of the caller's products and leaves the rest as they are. Through `is_active` it also withdraws a product, or puts a withdrawn one back on sale.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.who: A merchant allowed to trade, as for creating, and only on its own products.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.id: The product's numeric `id`, from the create answer, `GET /api/v1/products/mine`, or the public list or detail. A withdrawn product is found too.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.sku: Optional. May repeat the product's SKU (trimmed, not blank); any other value is refused.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.title: Optional. Same rule as at create; `null` is refused.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.descrip: Optional. Same rule as at create; `null` empties it.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.price: Optional. Same rule as at create; `null` is refused.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.image_u: Optional. Same rule as at create; `null` or an empty string removes the image.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.categor: Optional. An existing category's `id`; `null` is refused.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.is_acti: Optional. JSON `true` or `false`, nothing else. `false` withdraws the product from sale and, after the next sync, from search; `true` puts it back.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.field.weight_: Optional. Same rule as at create; `null` is refused, so a weight cannot be removed once set.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.updated: The product as it now stands, every field. Search reflects the change after its next sync.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.invalid: A field sent breaks its rule; only the first is reported. Fields are checked before identity is asked and before the product is looked up, so this answer says nothing about the product.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.unknownC: `category_id` is well formed, but no category has it.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.skuChang: `sku` differs from the product's SKU. A new SKU is a new product: create it, and withdraw this one if it should no longer sell.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.notMerch: Identity knows no merchant for this account. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.mayNotSe: The account's merchant may not trade: it awaits approval, or it is suspended or closed. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.notOwner: The product belongs to another merchant. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.notFound: No product, on sale or withdrawn, has this `id`.
rest.catalog.updateProduct.case.identity: Catalog could not learn the merchant's standing from identity. Nothing was changed; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.summary: Withdraws one of the caller's products from sale. The product is kept, with its SKU: it is no longer listed or read by SKU, search drops it after its next sync, and `is_active` `true` on the update endpoint puts it back.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.who: A merchant allowed to trade, and only on its own products.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.field.id: The product's numeric `id`. A product already withdrawn is found too.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.case.withdraw: The product is withdrawn, or already was; repeating the request answers the same. No body.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.case.notMerch: Identity knows no merchant for this account. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.case.mayNotSe: The account's merchant may not trade: it awaits approval, or it is suspended or closed. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.case.notOwner: The product belongs to another merchant. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.case.notFound: No product, on sale or withdrawn, has this `id`.
rest.catalog.deleteProduct.case.identity: Catalog could not learn the merchant's standing from identity. Nothing was changed; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.
rest.catalog.listCategories.summary: Lists every category in one answer, in no guaranteed order.
rest.catalog.listCategories.who: Anyone. The endpoint does not read the `Authorization` header.
rest.catalog.listCategories.case.listed: Every category. A product's `category_id` is a category's `id`; product filters and search match its `slug`.
rest.catalog.getCategory.who: Anyone. The endpoint does not read the `Authorization` header.
rest.catalog.createCategory.summary: Creates a category that products can be filed under.
rest.catalog.createCategory.who: Admins only: the token's `role` must be `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Each request that passes the role check is recorded in catalog's audit log under the admin's account, with its outcome.
rest.catalog.createCategory.field.name: Required. Text, trimmed, not blank, at most 128 characters; no NUL character. Unique.
rest.catalog.createCategory.field.slug: Required. 1 to 128 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, taken as sent (not trimmed). Unique. Product filters and search match it.
rest.catalog.createCategory.case.created: The category. Its `id` is what products send as `category_id`.
rest.catalog.createCategory.case.invalid: `name` or `slug` is missing or breaks its rule. `name` is checked first, and only the first broken rule is reported.
rest.catalog.createCategory.case.notAdmi: The token is valid, but its `role` is not `admin`. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.createCategory.case.taken: Another category already has this name or this slug.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.summary: Replaces a category's name and slug; both must be sent.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.who: Admins only: the token's `role` must be `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Each request that passes the role check is recorded in catalog's audit log under the admin's account, with its outcome.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.field.name: Required. Same rule as at create.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.field.slug: Required. Same rule as at create.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.case.updated: The category as stored. Catalog's own product filter uses the new slug at once. When the name or the slug changed, every product filed under the category is sent to search again in the same transaction, so search's filters and facets use the new name and slug after its next sync.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.case.invalid: `name` or `slug` is missing or breaks its rule. Both are checked, `name` first, before the category is looked up.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.case.notAdmi: The token is valid, but its `role` is not `admin`. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.updateCategory.case.taken: Another category already has this name or this slug.
rest.catalog.deleteCategory.summary: Deletes a category that no product is filed under.
rest.catalog.deleteCategory.who: Admins only: the token's `role` must be `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Each request that passes the role check is recorded in catalog's audit log under the admin's account, with its outcome.
rest.catalog.deleteCategory.case.deleted: The category is gone. No body.
rest.catalog.deleteCategory.case.notAdmi: The token is valid, but its `role` is not `admin`. Nothing was changed.
rest.catalog.deleteCategory.case.inUse: Products are still filed under the category, withdrawn ones included; `product_count` says how many. Their merchants must move them to another category first. Nothing was deleted.
